mechanism_narrative: A sustained 1-month increase in the federal funds rate signals an ongoing monetary tightening cycle that raises discount rates for equity valuation, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS rises by ≥0.1pp over prior month, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate falls below 4.5% and remains below for one month, it signals labor market overheating that triggers aggressive monetary tightening, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of instances where UNRATE < 4.5% for one month, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in industrial production (INDPRO) and housing starts (HOUST) over the prior month indicates broad economic contraction, triggering risk-off sentiment and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of instances where INDPRO and HOUST both decline ≥0.5% over prior month, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During sustained monetary tightening (FEDFUNDS > 4.5% for ≥3 months), increased cost of capital reduces equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of instances during FEDFUNDS > 4.5% for 3 months, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 1-quarter increase in real GDP (GDPC1) signals robust economic expansion that supports corporate earnings growth, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 60% of instances where GDPC1 rises ≥0.5% over prior quarter, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When CPIAUCSL rises above 208.5, it signals accelerating inflation that triggers preemptive monetary tightening, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5d returns in > 60% of instances where CPIAUCSL > 208.5, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in retail sales (RSAFS) and payrolls (PAYEMS) over the prior month indicates strong consumer demand and labor market, fueling corporate earnings growth and producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 60% of instances where RSAFS and PAYEMS both rise ≥0.3% over prior month, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During labor market recovery (UNRATE > 5.0% and declining), improving job prospects boost consumer confidence and spending, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 60% of instances during UNRATE > 5.0% and declining, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.
